title: Establish release annotator and review retrospective process
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Release notes across teams are inconsistent in audience targeting, operational guidance, and localization readiness, causing rework, late redactions, and customer confusion. Goal: Define and pilot an "annotator" workflow and a lightweight retrospective cadence so every release has (1) an annotated internal draft for ops/CS/legal, (2) a pared customer-facing changelog with redaction metadata, and (3) a short post-release review capturing improvements for the next cycle. Deliverables: annotated release template, an editable Google Sheet + automation to populate changelog drafts from PR metadata, reviewer checklist and signoff flow, and a retrospective report template with measurable signals (time-to-publish, number of redactions, number of follow-up tickets).
tasks: Draft annotated release template: fields for audience, risk, rollback steps, owners, test coverage, telemetry links, and recommended customer wording
Prototype annotator in a Google Sheet and an Airtable view for pilots (auto-populate from PR labels and milestone)
Implement simple automation: GitHub Action to tag PRs and export change lines to the sheet (ENG-4821 dependency)
Create reviewer roster and signoff flows: PM -> ENG lead -> Design -> Legal -> Comms
Add gating checklist to launch playbook: annotated entry required before public changelog sync
Localize template and define minimal translation window for prioritized languages
Run two pilot releases (canary and GA) and collect metrics and feedback
Publish retrospective report and update playbook with at least 3 actionable changes
acceptance_criteria: Annotated template accepted by design and legal (signoff captured in comments)
Automation exports change lines for >= 80% of PRs in pilot releases
Reviewer signoff completes within target SLA (48h) in at least one pilot
Customer-facing changelog published within target window and matches redaction guidance
Retrospective identifies at least 3 improvements and owners assigned
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: aligned scope with Eng and Design. Agreed to pilot with two upcoming releases: runtime-1.18 canary and console-2026.03 cut.
2026-03-04 - Design review: DES request to add a short 'What this means for you' field for each changelog line. Action: Luca to update template.
2026-03-06 - Engineering scope note: Automation will reuse existing PR label conventions; ENG will allocate one engineer for 2 sprints (ENG-4821).
2026-03-09 - Legal flagged data-disclosure language for Private deployments. Legal review required for any change that mentions customer data handling. Added as gating item.
2026-03-12 - Pilot 1 (canary) results: automation captured 72% of PR lines; reviewer turnaround averaged 36h. Two follow-up tickets created for ambiguous 'breaking' labels.
2026-03-15 - Decision: proceed with pilot 2 and increase automation heuristics to include PR body scannables. Localizations to start after pilot 2 results.
risks: Engineering bandwidth: automation depends on ENG prioritization; if delayed, more manual work will be required
Legal gating could increase publish time for customer-facing notes
Localization delay: translations may push public changelog beyond target window
Overly prescriptive template may discourage contributors from filling entries, leading to poor coverage
decision_log: 2026-03-04 - Chose Google Sheet + Airtable prototype to accelerate pilots versus building UI (minimizes engineering lift)
2026-03-12 - Approved automation approach to mine PR labels and bodies; target 80% coverage before considering UI build
2026-03-15 - Decided retest pilots with improved heuristics; localization to be scoped only for top 3 customer languages in pilot 2
